title: Pattern Headings: Organs and Regions of the Body
summary: Pattern list of free-floating subdivisions for headings for internal or external parts of the human or animal body (organs, organ systems, tissues, anatomical regions, and parts divided by anatomical subdivisions such as Brain--Ventricles); pattern headings Foot and Heart. Subdivisions representing diseases, injuries or other pathological conditions may be further subdivided by the H 1150 diseases pattern; endnotes restrict --Muscles, --Permeability and --Ultrasonic imaging and route legal and class-of-persons further subdivisions to H 1154.5 and H 1100.
validation_rules: The category covers headings for internal or external parts of the human or animal body, including organs and organ systems, tissues, and anatomical regions (e.g. `Abdomen`, `Bill (Anatomy)`, `Central nervous system`, `Intestine, Small`, `Nails (Anatomy)`, `Nerves, Peripheral`, `Urinary organs`), and parts of the body divided by anatomical subdivisions (e.g. `Brain--Ventricles`, `Leg--Blood-vessels`). (H 1164, Types of headings)

Not covered: headings for cellular or subcellular constituents (e.g. `Erythrocytes`, `Sex chromosomes`) and the general headings `Human body`, `Organs (Anatomy)`, `Tissues`. (H 1164, Types of headings)
Any subdivision on the list is free-floating under any heading in the category if appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file. (H 1164, Conflicts)

Subdivisions representing diseases, injuries, or other pathological conditions (those marked with note 1, e.g. `--Abnormalities`, `--Abscess`, `--Cancer`, `--Diseases`, `--Fractures`, `--Necrosis`, `--Tumors`, `--Ulcers`, `--Wounds and injuries`, `--Surgery--Complications`) may be further subdivided by subdivisions from the H 1150 diseases pattern, e.g. `Heart--Diseases--Diagnosis`, `Foot--Wounds and injuries--Chiropractic treatment`. (H 1164, Special provision; note 1)
`--Muscles` is not established under `Heart`; use `Myocardium` for the muscular substance of the heart. (H 1164 note 2)
`--Permeability` is not established under `Heart` or `Foot`; use under other organs and regions as appropriate. (H 1164 note 3)
`--Ultrasonic imaging` is not used under `Brain` or `Heart`: use `Ultrasonic encephalography` for the brain and `Echocardiography` for the heart. (H 1164 note 6)

`--Radiography--Law and legislation` and `--Transplantation--Law and legislation` may be further subdivided by H 1154.5 (legal topics); `--Surgery--Patients` and `--Transplantation--Patients` by H 1100 (classes of persons). (H 1164 notes 4, 5)

`--Religious aspects` may be further subdivided by a religion or Christian denomination; each heading `[part of the body]--Religious aspects--[name of religion or denomination]` must be editorially established. See H 1998. (H 1164 note 7)

Only subdivisions marked (May Subd Geog) on the list may be followed by a geographic subdivision (e.g. `--Diseases`, `--Surgery`, `--Physiology`); unmarked ones (e.g. `--Anatomy`, `--Cytology`, `--Growth`, `--Metabolism`, `--Displacement`, `--Effect of space flight on`, `--Religious aspects`) may not. (H 1164 list)
Most `$v` form subdivisions on this list may also be used as `$x` topical subdivisions for works about the form. (H 1164, list note)
[LC practice] An exceptional variant form to be retained gets a UF reference from the free-floating form (H 195); otherwise propose a change (H 193). (H 1164, Conflicts)

sections.heading: NOTES
sections.text:
1. See H 1150 for further subdivisions used under diseases.
2. Not established under Heart. Use Myocardium for the muscular substance of the heart.
3. Not established under Heart or Foot. Use under other organs and regions of the body as appropriate.
4. See H 1154.5 for further subdivisions used under legal topics.
5. See H 1100 for further subdivisions used under classes of persons.
6. Not established under Heart. Use under parts of the body other than Brain and Heart. For ultrasonic imaging of the brain, use Ultrasonic encephalography; for ultrasonic imaging of the heart, use Echocardiography.
7. May be subdivided topically by a religion or Christian denomination. Editorially establish each heading of the type [part of the body]–Religious aspects–[name of religion or denomination]. For instructions on the use of the subdivision, see H 1998.

list.scope: Free-floating subdivisions under headings for internal or external parts of the human or animal body (organs, organ systems, tissues, anatomical regions), including parts divided by anatomical subdivisions (e.g. Brain--Ventricles); not cellular or subcellular constituents, nor Human body; Organs (Anatomy); Tissues.
list.pattern_category: organs and regions of the body
general_notes: Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file.  Subject authority records may exist for headings employing variant phrases or subdivisions equivalent to subdivisions on this list.

SPECIAL PROVISION:  Subdivisions on this list that represent diseases, injuries, or other pathological conditions, for example, –Abnormalities; –Abscess; –Cancer; –Diseases; –Fractures; –Necrosis; –Tumors; –Ulcers; –Wounds and injuries may be further subdivided, as appropriate, by subdivisions from the pattern list for diseases (H 1150).  Further subdivisions established in the subject authority file under Heart or Foot, for example, Heart–Diseases–Diagnosis and Foot–Wounds and injuries–Chiropractic treatment, have been removed from the list below.
Most form subdivisions coded $v in this list may also be used as topical subdivisions coded $x when assigned to works about the form (see H 1075, sec. 1.d.).
